subject: Observability & Evals follow-up — scope, success metrics, and action plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Observability & Evals — recap and next steps

Hi Oliver (and Priya),

Thanks for taking the time this morning — good first look at FinLytics' observability gaps. I wanted to capture what we agreed, confirm success criteria, and propose concrete next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. I attached the quick requirements spreadsheet you mentioned and a draft SLA for review.

Recap of pain points you shared:
- Sporadic latency spikes (p95 > 1.2s) affecting live scoring during end-of-day batch runs; root cause unknown.
- Two recent model rollouts caused silent quality regressions in production prompts. No clear way to tie model changes to UX regressions.
- Lack of centralized tracing across prompt->inference->post-process steps (sampling and prompt templating live in different services).
- Need cost visibility per feature (token-level cost attribution) to decide quantization vs. model swap tradeoffs.

Concrete success criteria we discussed (proposal):
1) Traceability: end-to-end traces that link a user request through our SDK to the model invocation and downstream post-processing (sample spans + request IDs).
2) Regression detection: automated evals running nightly against a golden prompt set with alerting on delta thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR-style metrics + human-reviewed fail rate > 5%).
3) Observability surface: a dashboard showing p50/p95 latency, token cost per call, success-rate by route, and per-model quality variance over time.
4) Rollouts: Canary deploys with automatic rollback trigger based on combined latency + quality guardrails.

Proposed next steps and owners (rough timeline):
- Laura: sketch initial dashboard tile set and a recommended sampling strategy (ETA: Thu 2026-10-07).
- Neha: propose regression alert thresholds and runbook for false positives (ETA: Thu 2026-10-07).
- Karthik (me): draft a model rollout policy template and a short integration checklist for tracing hooks (ETA: Tue 2026-10-05).
- FinLytics (Oliver/Priya): share a representative golden prompt set (5–10 prompts per critical flow) and an anonymized production sample (csv) if possible (ETA: Wed 2026-10-06).

Questions we had outstanding:
- Do you prefer pull-based nightly evals or a streaming/near-real-time regression monitor for high-risk routes?
- Are there hard SLAs for specific endpoints during end-of-day runs (we heard "near real-time is ok except for scoring which needs < 2s p95").

If that matches your view, I'll convert these into a one-page mutual action plan and book a 30-minute follow-up with Laura and Neha next week to go through the dashboard wireframe.

Thanks again — looking forward to the golden prompts and sample data.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: finlytics-observability-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet of metrics & sample rows)
Attachment: redwood-proposed-sla-v1.pdf (draft SLA for review)

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finlytics.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@finlytics.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & Evals — recap and next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. This maps to our notes and is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: scoring endpoint requirement is p95 < 2.0s during normal load, but during the batch window we currently tolerate up to 3.0s for non-interactive tasks. The p95 > 1.2s spikes I mentioned earlier are in interactive routes and are user-visible.
- Regression signal: we already run a very small nightly eval (hand-curated prompts) but it looks siloed; we'd like Redwood's evals to be the canonical source and to include automated thresholds + a human review queue.
- Golden prompts: attached 8 prompts across three flows (search-summ, compliance-filter, risk-score). We redacted PII.

We're fine with nightly evals + a lightweight near-real-time monitor for our top 3 routes.

I attached the golden prompts (csv) and a short CSV export of anonymized request traces for last week — columns: request_id, route, latency_ms, model, tokens_in, tokens_out. Let us know if the schema doesn't line up.

Oliver
Director of Engineering
FinLytics

Subject: Internal: FinLytics discovery — quick action plan (please confirm owners)

Laura / Neha — looping you both in with Oliver's confirmation and the attached sample data. High level asks (repeat): dashboard tiles, regression alerting, tracing hooks, rollout guardrails, and token-cost visibility.

Please see my proposed owners/tactics — tweak as you see fit: 
- Laura: dashboard wireframe + sampling strategy. Plan to include: p50/p95 latency by route, token-cost heatmap (by feature), model quality trend (nightly eval score). Consider a toggle for showing only canary traffic.
- Neha: define concrete alert thresholds (suggested: nightly eval delta > 4% absolute failure rate or per-prompt score drop > 0.07 LLR) and a human-review triage flow. Draft a short runbook for on-call.
- Karthik: draft rollout policy: canary sizes, rollback thresholds, and a small checklist for SDK tracing integration (span naming, request_id propagation, sample rate).

Proposed timeline: internal deliverables by next Thu (2026-10-07). I will book a 30m sync with Oliver & Priya for Fri 2026-10-08 to walk the wireframe and runbook.

Action items (short):
- Laura: first wireframe PNG + sample query to populate tiles (ETA 2026-10-07).
- Neha: alert thresholds doc + runbook draft (ETA 2026-10-07).
- Karthik: rollout policy + tracing checklist (ETA 2026-10-05).
- Oliver: confirm the anonymized sample is representative and give access to a staging endpoint if possible (Oliver/Priya ETA 2026-10-06).

Thanks — please confirm owners and the proposed meeting time.

—
Karthik
